::: {.lead}
Today you format a real notice in Word, like in a lab. Each experiment has
two parts. **Part A** is in Word on the lab computer. **Part B** is on a
simulator of the interactive lesson: on paper, scan its QR code; on the
screen, click its link. After each step, write your result in its box. At
the end, copy your key results into the table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with Word (the desktop app, or Word on the
  web at `office.com`) and the two start files.
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer with Word.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

{{< start-files >}}

## Experiment 1 · Text and paragraph formatting

**The idea:** **text formatting** (font, size, bold, italic, colour:
**Home › Font**) changes only the text that you select. **Paragraph
formatting** (alignment, line spacing: **Home › Paragraph**) changes the
whole paragraph: a click inside it is enough. Use bold for one or two
important things only.

**Aim:** see which commands change only the selected text, and which
change a whole paragraph.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. Open `book-fair-start.docx` in Word (click **Enable Editing** if a
   yellow bar asks). In the last line, *Entry to the fair is free for
   everyone.*, select only the word **free** and click **Bold** (Home ›
   Font). Then click in the same line, select nothing, and click
   **Center** (Home › Paragraph).

   {{< record "Bold changed … ; Center moved …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Bold** changed only the word **free**: text formatting changes only
   the selection. **Center** moved **the whole line**: paragraph formatting
   changes the whole paragraph, and a click inside it is enough.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Only the selected text, or the whole paragraph? Sort the commands.

   Only the selected text (Home › Font)
   :   Bold

       Why: It changes only the letters that you select.

   :   Font size

       Why: A text command: select first.

   :   Font colour

       Why: A text command too.

   The whole paragraph (Home › Paragraph)
   :   Center

       Why: A click inside the line is enough: the whole line moves.

   :   Line spacing

       Why: It changes the space between all the lines of the paragraph.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-04/sims/format-lab.html" poster="../../week-04/sims/format-lab.png" title="Format Lab: text and paragraph formatting" >}}

2. In **Format Lab**, do the five jobs of the library notice: the title in
   size 20, bold, centred and orange; the text with line spacing 1.15; only
   the last line bold. Which jobs did you do with a click inside a
   paragraph, without selecting text?

   {{< record "With a click inside the paragraph: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Centred** and **line spacing 1.15**: they are paragraph formatting
   (Home › Paragraph). Size, bold and colour are text formatting (Home ›
   Font): you select the text first.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   In Format Lab, the title must be centred. What must you do first?

   - [x] Click inside the title line: Center works on the whole paragraph.

     Why: Paragraph formatting needs only a click inside the paragraph.

   - [ ] Select every letter of the title.

     Why: That is needed for text formatting, like a colour.

   - [ ] Select the whole notice.

     Why: Then all the lines are centred, not only the title.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · Styles and headings

**The idea:** a **style** is saved formatting with a name: **Title**,
**Heading 1**, **Heading 2**, **Normal** (Home › Styles). Change a style
once, and all the text with it changes. **View › Navigation Pane** shows
the headings as a map. A heading made "by hand" (bold and big) is normal
text for Word.

**Aim:** give headings a style, and see what a style does for the whole
document.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. Click in the first line, *Book Fair at the College Library*, and choose
   the style **Title** (Home › Styles). Then give the style **Heading 1**
   to the four headings: *When and where*, *What you can bring*, *How to
   swap a book* and *Prices*.

   {{< record "How do the four headings look now?" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Bigger and in a colour (often blue). All four look the same, because
   they have the same style.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   How do the four headings look now?

   - [x] all the same: bigger and in a colour

     Why: They have the same style, Heading 1.

   - [ ] each one a little different

     Why: One style gives the same look to all of them.

   - [ ] like the normal text

     Why: Heading 1 makes them bigger and coloured.
   :::

2. In **Home › Styles**, right-click **Heading 1** and choose **Modify**.
   Choose a green font colour and click **OK**.

   {{< record "What happens to the headings?" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **All four headings turn green at once.** You changed the style one
   time, and all the text with this style changed.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   You change **Heading 1** to green one time. What happens?

   - [x] All four headings turn green at once.

     Why: A style changes all the text that has it.

   - [ ] Only the heading where you clicked turns green.

     Why: You changed the style, not one heading.

   - [ ] The title turns green too.

     Why: The title has the style Title, not Heading 1.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-04/sims/style-lab.html" poster="../../week-04/sims/style-lab.png" title="Style Lab: styles and the Navigation Pane" >}}

3. In **Style Lab**, give each line of the class trip plan its style:
   Title, Heading 1, Heading 2 or Normal. Look at the Navigation Pane. How
   many headings does it show?

   {{< record "The Navigation Pane shows … headings" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **4 headings**: *The plan* and *What to bring* (Heading 1), *Morning*
   and *Afternoon* (Heading 2). The title and the normal text are not in
   the pane.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="4" unit="headings" hint="Count the lines with Heading 1 or Heading 2."}
   The plan has two lines with Heading 1 and two with Heading 2. How many
   headings does the Navigation Pane show?

   Why: The pane shows the headings only: 2 + 2 = 4. The title and the normal text are not in it.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · A list and a table

**The idea:** a **bulleted list** (Home › Paragraph › Bullets) is for things
in no order; a **numbered list** (Numbering) is for steps in an order. A
**table** (Insert › Table) puts information in rows and columns; its first
row, the **header row**, names the columns. **Tab** in the last cell adds a
row. Never make columns with spaces.

**Aim:** choose bullets or numbers, and put information in a table.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. Look at the three lines under *What you can bring* and the three lines
   under *How to swap a book*. One group needs **Bullets**, the other
   **Numbering** (Home › Paragraph). Decide, and do it.

   {{< record "Bullets for … ; numbers for … , because …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Bullets** for the things to bring: they have no order. **Numbering**
   for the steps of the swap: they have an order (first, second, third).
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Bullets or numbering? Sort the lists.

   Bullets: no order
   :   the three things you can bring

       Why: Things in no special order.

   :   the names of the guests

       Why: Names have no order of steps.

   Numbering: an order
   :   the three steps to swap a book

       Why: Steps come one after the other.

   :   the steps of a recipe

       Why: The order of a recipe matters.
   :::

2. Click at the end of the line *Prices* and press Enter. The prices are:
   novel 3 JD, dictionary 5 JD, notebook 1 JD. Insert a table (Insert ›
   Table) with 2 columns and the rows that you need, with a header row.
   Type *Book* and *Price (JD)* in the first row, then the three books.

   {{< record "My table has … columns and … rows" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **2 columns and 4 rows**: 1 header row (*Book*, *Price (JD)*) and 3 rows
   for the three items.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="4" unit="rows" hint="One row for the headings, and one row for each item."}
   How many rows does the price table need, with its header row?

   Why: 1 header row + 3 items = 4 rows, in 2 columns: Book and Price (JD).
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-04/sims/list-table-lab.html" poster="../../week-04/sims/list-table-lab.png" title="List and Table Lab: bullets, numbers and a table" >}}

3. In **List and Table Lab**, choose bullets or numbers for each list, then
   build the table of the bus plan. How many columns and rows does the
   table need?

   {{< record "The bus plan: … columns and … rows" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **2 columns and 5 rows**: the header row (*Time*, *Activity*) and one
   row for each of the 4 times (9:00, 10:00, 13:00, 16:00).
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="5" unit="rows" hint="One header row, and one row for each time."}
   The bus plan has 4 times, each with an activity. How many rows does its
   table need, with the header row?

   Why: 1 header row + 4 times = 5 rows, in 2 columns: Time and Activity.
   :::

## Experiment 4 · A picture

**The idea:** **Insert › Pictures** adds a picture. Drag a **corner** to
change its size: the shape stays right. **Text wrapping** (Layout Options):
*In Line with Text* (the picture is like a big letter in a line) or
*Square* (the text flows around it). **Alt text** says in a few words what
the picture shows; a screen reader reads it aloud.

**Aim:** add a picture, and let the text flow around it.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. Click at the start of the text *The college library holds …*. Choose
   **Insert › Pictures › This Device** and open `books.png`. Make it
   smaller with a **corner** handle. Then click **Layout Options** (the
   small button next to the picture) and choose **Square**.

   {{< record "First the picture sits … ; with Square, the text …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   First the picture sits **in the line**, like a very big letter (*In
   Line with Text*). With **Square**, the text **flows around the
   picture**.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   With **Square**, what does the text do?

   - [x] It flows around the picture.

     Why: With Square, the picture and the text share the lines.

   - [ ] It moves under the picture.

     Why: That is how a picture in line with the text looks.

   - [ ] It goes behind the picture.

     Why: Square puts the text next to the picture, not behind it.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-04/sims/notice-maker.html" poster="../../week-04/sims/notice-maker.png" title="Notice Maker: Huda's Family Day notice" kind="game" >}}

2. Play **Notice Maker**: make Huda's Family Day notice with the six jobs.
   The last two jobs are for the park picture: Square wrapping and alt
   text. Which alt text did you write?

   {{< record "My alt text for the park picture" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good answer: a few words that say what the picture shows, for example
   **"A green park with trees"**. Not the file name, and not only
   "picture".
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which alt text is good for the park picture?

   - [x] A green park with trees

     Why: Alt text says in a few words what the picture shows.

   - [ ] park.jpg

     Why: A file name does not say what the picture shows.

   - [ ] Picture

     Why: Every picture is a picture: say what it shows.
   :::
